evidence: Agent confirmed test/config.test.js:695 only exercised the unknown-preset arm, so the new inputKeys.credential throw was unexecuted; 6b88029 added refusal cases for every illegal shape plus the shipped-table check.
guidance_note: When adding a new throw arm to a load-time validator, add a refusal test for each illegal shape in the same commit.

evidence: The reviewer predicted a 401 on every judge call, but the agent's live curl with Bearer returned 200, and the committed baseline was scored end to end with --matcher llm through callJudge, which aborts on any non-200, so a 401 could not have produced it. The only evidence is the agent's report of that curl run; the packet holds nothing independent of it.

The reviewer flagged its own claim as unverified. The agent's curl sent thinking:{type:'disabled'} to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 on api.anthropic.com and got 200 with a text block, and the baseline was scored through the same body.
The untouched 'Running it in CI' line still said 'a few dollars and around an hour', but the new baseline has costPerFullRunUsd: null and runs 20 serial replays at 13-27 min each; a19c2fe rewrote it.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a measured number (cost, runtime), grep the docs for every other statement of that number and update them in the same commit.

evidence: 100000*60*1000 = 6e9 is above setTimeout's 2147483647 limit, so the timer fires almost at once; 6bce6c7 bounds --job-timeout at 35791 and tests both sides of the boundary.
guidance_note: When a CLI number is converted into a setTimeout delay, bound it at parse time against the 2^31-1 ms ceiling.

evidence: renderReport never received outRoot, so the 'Next:' hint said plain `node eval/baseline.js`, whose --out-dir defaults to eval/out, while the README's own step 3 passes --out-dir; the old test only matched /eval\/baseline\.js/.
guidance_note: When a tool prints a follow-up command, build it from the run's actual arguments and have the test assert the interpolated path.

evidence: In the diff hunk, `Option --${rawName} requires a value.` prints `--n` for input `-n`. The fix resolves the canonical name once and uses it for the lookup and both messages.
guidance_note: When a parser claims to mirror a sibling parser, diff the two before shipping instead of relying on the claim.

evidence: README line 288 still said baselines are tagged with 'the exact main SHA', while the new Provenance note says ebccbd4 is deliberately not a main commit. The agent notes that 4a9c2d1 had already fixed the same wording in baseline.js's help text but missed this copy.
guidance_note: When rewording a fact in code help text, grep the docs for the old phrasing and fix every restatement in the same commit.

evidence: The `queue.push(job); return;` in the hunk ends the only lane on the first failure, so the default single-lane run abandons the whole queue. The agent rejected credential-exhaustion sniffing (no reliable exit signature exists) and the lane-count branch, and replaced both with a per-lane attempted set, mutation-checked by two tests. That rule later left the README stale (F23) and a multi-lane completion-order race open (F35).
guidance_note: When changing a scheduling rule, update every doc that describes the old rule and test the multi-lane interleavings, not only the single-lane case.

evidence: `setTimeout(() => signalGroup('SIGKILL'), 20000).unref()` in the hunk is never captured, so the close handler cannot cancel it. 6bce6c7 captured it and cleared it in close and error, but added no test (the gap F22 raised).
guidance_note: When fixing a timer-cleanup bug, make the signaller injectable and add a regression test in the same commit.

evidence: The agent verified PROVIDERS.codex.engine === 'codex', so the hardcoded middle segment 'claude-code' is right only for the current auto target. 65f7dcc derived it, but the claim that the -n guard would catch a missing engine field was false (F20), and the 'auto' literal in the same function was left in place (F19).
guidance_note: When de-literalizing one segment of a derivation, audit every remaining literal in the same function and check that the guard rejects interpolated 'undefined', not just empty strings.

evidence: logDir = path.join(outRoot,'logs') made logs/ match the documented `freeze-<sha>/*/` glob, and the agent confirmed that shape on disk; the logs moved to a sibling `${outRoot}-logs`, one of the reviewer's two offered fixes.
guidance_note: Before documenting a glob over a tool's output root, list what the tool actually writes under that root.

evidence: The plan was to raise timeout-minutes to cover the worst case, but 20 x 13-27 min is 260-540 min against GitHub's 360-min ceiling. The agent set 350 and stated the shortfall in both places instead, which is an honest partial fix; the real fix was correctly left as structural.
guidance_note: When re-pinning a CI gate to a slower engine, redo the job's runtime arithmetic against the platform ceiling before merging.

evidence: resolveLanes ran before planJobs, so a status-check run at the target N demanded an unset credential. The fix derives the lane names from the planned jobs, giving an empty list when there is nothing to run.
guidance_note: Order credential resolution after work planning so a zero-work invocation never demands a secret.

evidence: buildProviderInputs, which the original PR removed, survived only in this comment. The agent described the downstream path instead of naming a symbol in another file. This is original-PR drift, not caused by any review fix.
guidance_note: When deleting a function, grep the repo for its name, comments included, before pushing.

evidence: listRunDirs is a new export whose missing-dir-returns-[] contract freeze-suite's census depends on, and no test called it; d4ff3c4 added a real temp-tree suite.
guidance_note: When extracting and exporting a function whose contract differs from its predecessor's, add a direct test of the differing arm.

evidence: The extractText and callJudge comments still justified the code by DeepSeek and flash-model quirks after the original PR switched the judge to Anthropic Haiku. Both were rewritten to the general contract.
guidance_note: When swapping a provider or model, grep the file for comments naming the old one and restate them as provider-neutral contracts.

evidence: The hunk shows the comparison using BASELINE_SCHEMA while the message hardcodes 'v2'. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted, also fixing the test regex pinned to the same literal.
guidance_note: When introducing a named constant, replace every literal copy of its value, error messages and test assertions included.

evidence: F11's fix (65f7dcc) rewrote default_engine to derive the engine segment but left `PROVIDER_ALIASES.auto` as a literal assumption about action.yml's default in the same function. The agent also found the unanchored awk would misread PROVIDER's description line and built one anchored reader.
guidance_note: When fixing one hardcoded fact in a derivation function, trace every input of that function back to its source of truth before pushing.

evidence: F11's reply claimed 'a missing engine field fails loudly at freeze time', but `${row.engine}` interpolates the literal 'undefined', which passes the -n guard. The agent moved validation of engine and defaultModel into assertProvidersSafe for every consumer instead of string-matching 'undefined'.
guidance_note: Before claiming a guard catches a missing field, run it against a row with the field deleted.

evidence: credentialInputFor's direct PROVIDERS[provider] lookup is in the original round-0 code (F14's hunk shows it). The agent reproduced the 'does not define auto' failure live and added one resolveProviderName/providerSpec definition instead of a third inline copy, leaving the new path untested (F37) and an unswept copy in local-review.js (F32).
guidance_note: When introducing a canonical helper for a repeated expression, grep the repo for every remaining copy and add a test at each migrated call site.

evidence: The reviewer names it directly: 'the timer-cleanup fix from an earlier review round ... has no regression test protecting it'. The agent split superviseSpawn out, injected the signaller, and mutation-checked that reverting clearTimeout(escalation) turns a test red.
guidance_note: When fixing a bug in effectful code, make the effect injectable and add the regression test in the same fix commit.

evidence: The README bullet 'a lane stops at its first failure' describes the runLane behaviour that F9's fix (6bce6c7) replaced with the attempted-set rule; the agent concedes 'this documents the behavior 6bce6c7 replaced'.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a behaviour the README describes, grep the docs for the old rule's wording in the same commit.

evidence: 'exactly three things' heads four bullets. The 'deadline per replay' bullet was in the original branch (the round-0 code already had the deadline), so this is original drift, not a review fix.
guidance_note: When adding an item to an enumerated list, update any count stated in its lead-in sentence.

evidence: With detached:true the replays leave the terminal's foreground group, and there was no SIGINT handler, so Ctrl-C orphaned them. The fix added a module-scoped mutable registry while citing no-shared-mutable-globals as its justification, and it sent a single SIGTERM with no escalation (F31).
guidance_note: When adding a shutdown path to a file that already has a SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL escalation, reuse that escalation rather than writing a one-shot signal.

evidence: Every planner test hand-built {name, dir, completed}, bypassing censusCases. 31ce1cf added temp-tree tests including a dir-name/manifest-name mismatch, mutation-checked.
guidance_note: When a function joins two sources of truth, write a fixture in which the join keys can disagree.

evidence: resolveConfigChain is the only caller that passes baseUrl through resolveProviderConfig, and no test covered it; 31ce1cf added the zai override test plus the claude-subscription pinned-host case.
guidance_note: When replacing a hand-written mapping with a generic loop, test every field the loop carries for at least one row that declares it.

evidence: The only reasoning test ran through claude-subscription, whose inputKeys declares no reasoning key, so no positive-path value was ever threaded. The table-driven FIELD sweep added in 31ce1cf left model out, which F40 then raised.
guidance_note: When building a table-driven sweep over a row's fields, include every field the rows declare and mutation-test by deleting one mapping per row.

evidence: F20's fix extended assertProvidersSafe to engine and defaultModel but skipped credentialInput, the env-var name read in resolveProviderConfig; the agent calls it 'the more important half of the pair I added last round'. Fixed in c564e73/bd1b47b.
guidance_note: When tightening a row validator, list every field a consumer reads off the row and validate all of them, not just the ones the finding named.

evidence: The NO_PROVIDER fallback was in the original change (the round-1 summary mentions it), and no test passed an unknown provider. bd1b47b added typo and absent-provider tests checked against PROVIDER_NAMES.
guidance_note: When adding a fallback sentinel for an unknown key, test the unknown-key path and the error message it produces.

evidence: The hunk shows F25's handler doing `for (const pid of inFlight) signalGroup(pid, 'SIGTERM'); process.exit(...)`, with no SIGKILL escalation, though superviseSpawn treats SIGTERM-ignoring trees as real. The agent concedes the fix 'sent one fire-and-forget SIGTERM'.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a second kill path, reuse the file's existing kill escalation rather than writing a reduced copy.

evidence: F21's fix introduced providerSpec as the one name-to-row lookup but missed the hand-rolled `PROVIDER_ALIASES[requested] || requested` in local-review.js's --base-url guard; the agent says 'a block I did not think to look at because this PR had not touched it'.
guidance_note: When introducing a canonical helper, grep the whole repo for the expression it replaces, not just files the PR already touched.

evidence: The unhandled stream 'error' would crash the whole suite. The agent logged it rather than failing the job, rightly noting a log-write error says nothing about the replay's outcome. The createWriteStream line dates from round 0 and only moved into superviseSpawn under F22's split, so the logic is not fix-caused.
guidance_note: Attach an 'error' listener to every stream you create in a long-running supervisor.

evidence: `opts[name] = value` accepts '' and path.resolve('') is the CWD, so --out= silently retargets to the CWD. The one refusal at the shared assignment point covers every option, and that parse code is original round-0 code.
guidance_note: When writing an arg parser, reject empty option values at the single assignment point.

evidence: F9's attempted-set rule claims 'healthy lanes keep draining', but a lane exits on an empty queue while a peer may still requeue a job. The agent added a makeLaneGroup rendezvous held across the requeue and confirmed the test goes red without it.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a concurrent scheduling rule, test a two-lane interleaving where the healthy lane finishes first.

evidence: The agent agreed with the diagnosis but showed runCli is untouched by the PR, and that a spawnSync timeout cannot be detached, so it would reap run-case.js and leave the quota-burning grandchildren running. It filed zai-copirate-eval-harness-77c instead of shipping a false fix.
guidance_note: When re-pinning a gate to an engine that can stall, list every spawn path the gate uses and check each for a deadline.

evidence: F21's fix (5986a9a) changed credentialInputFor to use providerSpec and was verified only by a live run, with no regression test. The flagged commit c564e73 only adds the credentialInput check, so the real cause is F21's untested fix.
guidance_note: When a fix repairs a bug you reproduced live, turn that reproduction into a test in the same commit.

evidence: F22's fix split superviseSpawn out and tested it, but left runReplay's job-to-argv/env mapping, now its only job, untested. 51c5cc8 extracted a pure replaySpawnSpec and tested that the lane credential overrides an inherited env var.
guidance_note: When decomposing a function to test one half, test the other half in the same commit.

evidence: The agent traced the rename to bd1b47b, the round-3 fix commit for F29-F35, where `git add -A` swept in a stray installer edit. It confirmed install.sh:226 still emits 'AI Code Review' and reverted the rename in 1fd8580.
guidance_note: Stage fix commits by explicit path, never `git add -A`, and review `git diff --cached --stat` before committing.

evidence: The FIELD sweep added for F28 left zaiModel uncovered. The agent mutation-tested the suggested fix: with model in FIELD, deleting zaiModel still passed 104/104, because the sweep reads `declared` from the table it tests. So it asserted the model override unconditionally per row instead.
guidance_note: When writing a table-driven test, take the expected set from outside the system under test, and mutation-test by deleting one entry.

evidence: F31's shutdownInFlight signalled only groups already in flight, while runLane's loop kept spawning through the 20s grace window. The fix (`group.stopped ? -1 : findIndex`) is sound and mutation-verified, but it is still a flag checked in the loop, so the dataflow citation dresses a conditional as a value.
guidance_note: When adding interrupt handling to a scheduler, stop new work from starting before signalling in-flight work, and test both.

narrative: A large eval-harness PR that ran into the 5-round review cap. Rounds 0-1 raised real original-PR defects, most accepted with sound fixes. From round 2 on, a growing share of findings were remainders of earlier fixes: the guard claimed by F11's fix did not catch 'undefined', F20's validator extension missed credentialInput, the interrupt handler added for F25 lacked escalation and then let lanes keep spawning, and fix commits shipped without regression tests (F10, F21). By round 4 all five findings were fix-caused, including a stray generated-file edit swept in by `git add -A` in a fix commit.
guidance_observations: Several fixes were verified live but shipped without a regression test (F10, F21), and the next round then asked for exactly those tests; writing the test in the fix commit would have saved findings.
Fixes that introduced a canonical helper (providerSpec) or a validator extension were not followed by a repo-wide sweep for the remaining instances, producing same-gap findings one round later.
The agent's mutation-testing habit in later rounds was strong and caught two of its own vacuous tests (F35, F41) and a reviewer cure that would not have worked (F40).
Staging round-3 fixes with `git add -A` pulled an unreviewed generated-file edit into the PR.

evidence: composeSummary leads review.summary with the scout summary in both modes, and the agent confirmed renderRepoReport posts it (src/report.js:56). The repo-mode branch in the hunk told the scout only about workers; efe072f added the second reader.
guidance_note: When a contract string varies by mode, trace each mode's output to every sink before writing the per-mode text.

evidence: The hunk removes the per-worker `**scope** — summary` line, while review.js:60 still named it as a sink of the single-line stamp; the comment was trimmed to the sinks that remain.
guidance_note: When deleting a rendering, grep for comments that cite it as a reason for code elsewhere.

evidence: In PR mode the scout now writes a change narrative, but workerFocusText still labelled it 'Structural context from the planning pass'; the agent took the reviewer's mode-neutral option and updated the test asserting the old label.
guidance_note: When changing what a producer emits, check the labels its consumers wrap around that output.

narrative: A small PR moving summary authorship to the scout. Round 0 found three real drift issues the original change left behind: an undisclosed second reader in repo mode, a stale sink comment, and a label that no longer described its content. All three were fixed in one commit and round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: All three findings were leftovers the original change could have caught by grepping for consumers and comments that reference the changed output.
